title.narrative: Activity under preparation Support to Bangladesh Railway for Capacity Building on Green Project Development and Electrification.

description.narrative: The proposed action aims to strengthen the institutional and technical capacity of Bangladesh Railway (BR) and the Ministry of Railways (MoR) to plan, implement, and operate modern, sustainable, and energy¿efficient railway systems. With a budget of EUR 2.5 million under the transport sector, the action directly contributes to Bangladesh¿s national development priorities and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 5, 7, 8, 10, 11, and 13).BR operates a 3,100 km network across 43 districts (out of 64) and is central to the country¿s ambition to shift from road¿dominated transport to greener, safer, and more efficient rail mobility. The railway network is composed of Meter gauge and Broad gauge, sometimes dual gauge. The government¿s strategic documents including the National Land Transport Policy, the Integrated Multi¿modal Transport Policy (IMTP), and the Railway Master Plan 2016¿2045, prioritise network modernisation, gauge unification, electrification, multimodal integration, and improved service quality. The European Union (EU), through the European Investment Bank and other instruments, is already supporting major infrastructure investments along the Dhaka¿Chattogram¿Cox¿s Bazar corridor, including rolling stock procurement, dual¿gauge conversion, and planned electrification of key commuter and freight routes.Despite these investments, BR faces significant capacity gaps in modern project preparation, electrification planning, environmental management, and sustainable operations. Many existing practices are outdated, and staff require exposure to EU standards, digital tools, and green railway concepts. The action addresses these gaps through three mutually reinforcing components:Component 1 ¿ Railway Electrification and Green Concepts: This component enhances BR¿s technical expertise in electrification technologies, signalling, interoperability (between gauge systems and possibly for regional interconnection with India), safety, sustainable railway design, energy efficiency, and environmental safeguards. Training, workshops, peer exchanges, and study tours will expose staff to European best practices. A key output is the strengthened ability to develop a national framework for railway electrification, including standards, guidelines, and regulatory references adapted to Bangladesh¿s context.Component 2 ¿ Feasibility, Design & Development Project Proposals (DPPs): This component builds BR¿s capacity to prepare feasibility studies, technical designs, and DPPs aligned with EU sustainability criteria. Staff will learn to integrate lifecycle cost analysis, environmental safeguards, resilience measures, and green design principles into project documentation, ensuring future electrification projects are bankable, technically sound, and environmentally responsible.Component 3 ¿ Implementation and Operation: This component strengthens BR¿s ability to apply sustainable practices during procurement, construction, operation, and maintenance. It promotes renewable energy integration, optimised maintenance systems, digital energy monitoring tools, and EU¿aligned operational guidelines.
